attempted_claim: Consider the focusing 3D cubic NLS i∂_t u + Δu + |u|^2 u = 0 on R^3 with H^1 data, Q the radial positive ground state of -Q + ΔQ + Q^3 = 0. Let ψ be real-valued, radial, H^1 (Schwartz), strictly decreasing in r=|x|, ψ not identically 0, and set α_0 = ||Q||_{Ḣ^{1/2}} / ||ψ||_{Ḣ^{1/2}}, u_{0,α} = α ψ. Prove or disprove: the H^1 solution u_α scatters in H^1 in both time directions if 0 < α < α_0, and blows up in finite time in both time directions (T_± finite with ||∇u_α(t)||_{L^2} → ∞) if α > α_0, with no additional mass-energy, variance, or phase hypothesis?
decisive_failure: No rigorous proof or disproof of the two-sided H^{1/2}-threshold dichotomy was obtained. All ground-state and profile computations are numerical evidence with truncation and quadrature error, not theorems, and the Holmer-Roudenko plus virial routes were shown to be silent at the threshold locus rather than refuting or confirming the claim.
